sections.h2: What written notice comes before a Minnesota eviction for unpaid rent?
sections.html:
A landlord must give a written notice that lets the tenant cure the debt for 14 days before filing an eviction for unpaid rent or other money owed under the lease. Some local governments require a longer period, and the longer local period controls. The rule is Minn. Stat. 504B.321, subd. 1a.

The notice has to contain specific items, and a court dismisses the later case without prejudice, and expunges the file, if the landlord fails to attach a required notice to the complaint.

  • The total amount due, with an accounting that separates unpaid rent, late fees, and other charges.
  • The name and address of the person authorized to receive rent and fees for the landlord.
  • A statement that the tenant may seek legal help, with a pointer to Legal Aid and LawHelpMN.org.
  • A statement on applying for financial help through the county or Tribal social services office, MNBenefits.mn.gov, or the United Way line at 2-1-1 or 800-543-7709.
  • A statement that the landlord can file a case if the tenant neither pays nor moves out within 14 days of the notice date.

The landlord or an agent must deliver the notice personally or by first class mail to the tenant at the rental address. When a county agency receives a copy, it treats the notice as verification of the emergency for rental assistance and may not ask the tenant for more proof.

sections.h2: How much notice does a month-to-month tenant get in Minnesota?
sections.html:
A tenancy at will ends with written notice at least as long as the gap between rent due dates or three months, whichever is shorter. A tenant who pays monthly is therefore entitled to one month, and a tenant who pays weekly is entitled to one week. Minn. Stat. 504B.135 lets either side end the tenancy this way.

When a tenant stays after the lease term ends, section 504B.141 says no tenancy longer than the shortest rent interval of the expired lease is implied for urban property unless the landlord expressly agrees. Holding over after a lease ends, or after a notice to quit, is itself a ground for eviction under section 504B.285.

Two statutes cover fixed leases that renew themselves or carry different notice periods:

  • A landlord who wants to enforce an automatic renewal in a lease of two months or longer must send a written reminder, personally or by certified mail, 15 to 30 days before the tenant's deadline to give notice (504B.145).
  • A landlord's notice to quit or notice of a rent increase may not be shorter than the notice period the lease gives the tenant, and the tenant may choose either period when leaving (504B.147).

sections.h2: Which Minnesota notices are longer, shorter, or skipped?
sections.html:
The table lists the notice periods most likely to affect a house that is rented, foreclosed, or inherited. Each row has its own statute, so check which one fits the tenant's situation.

Common eviction and lease-ending notice periods in Minnesota
SituationNotice or timingStatute
Unpaid rent14 days, or longer if local law says so504B.321, subd. 1a
Tenancy at willRent interval or three months, whichever is less504B.135
Tenant in a foreclosed home, lease began after the mortgageAt least 90 days after redemption ends504B.285, subd. 1a
Tenant in a home cancelled under a contract for deedAt least two months504B.285, subd. 1b
Federally subsidized housing losing its subsidyOne year504B.255
Lease ended by the death of a tenantTwo months, effective on the last day of a month504B.265
Unlawful activity covenant breachedNo set notice period, right to possession voided504B.171

Source: Minnesota Statutes chapter 504B. The death-of-tenant notice can come from the landlord or from the tenant's personal representative, and it does not erase rent or restoration costs owed to that point.

sections.h2: Does a breach or a retaliation claim change a Minnesota notice?
sections.html:
A breach of the lease covenant against unlawful activity under section 504B.171 voids the tenant's right to possession, though rent and the other lease terms stay in force until the lease ends. A landlord who alleges this breach, or conduct that seriously endangers other residents, can seek an expedited hearing with an affidavit of specific facts.

Notice to quit can also be answered by a retaliation defense. A tenant who proves by a fair preponderance of the evidence that the notice was meant as a penalty for a good faith effort to enforce rights, or for reporting a code violation, defeats the case. If the notice was served within 90 days of the tenant's protected act, the landlord carries the burden of showing it was not retaliatory (504B.285, subd. 2).

Landlords who ask tenants to pay through a digital platform must offer another way to pay when the platform is down, with no fee. A landlord who starts an eviction or charges late fees after both options failed faces dismissal and the tenant's attorney fees, according to the Judicial Branch landlord FAQ.

sections.h2: What do these notice rules mean for someone selling a Minnesota house with tenants?
sections.html:
They set how long a tenant can stay and what paperwork must exist before anything is filed. A seller who wants a tenant out before closing should serve the correct notice first, because a missing or defective notice leads to dismissal and an expunged case.

  • If the owner has received notice of a mortgage foreclosure sale, any new residential lease can run only two months or the time left in the redemption period, whichever is less, and the tenant must be told in writing before signing. The civil penalty for skipping the written notice is $500 (504B.151).
  • The mortgagor's redemption period after the sheriff's sale is six months for most homes, with a 12-month period in listed cases such as land over 40 acres (580.23).
  • The lease and tenant deposit travel with the house. Ask the county recorder and your closing agent what the title company needs to see about leases and recorded judgments.

Forms for starting a case are on the Judicial Branch's landlord forms page, which also offers Minnesota Guide and File.

faqs.q: How many days notice does a Minnesota landlord have to give to evict for nonpayment?
faqs.a: Fourteen days from the notice date, unless a local rule sets a longer period. The notice must be delivered personally or by first class mail to the rental address and must list the amount due, an accounting, and the required legal help and financial help statements.

faqs.q: Can a Minnesota landlord evict without any written notice?
faqs.a: For unpaid rent, no. The complaint must have the written notice attached, or the court dismisses the case without prejudice and expunges the file. Holdover and lease breach cases have different rules, and a case under section 504B.171 can be expedited.

faqs.q: How much notice must a landlord give to end a month-to-month tenancy in Minnesota?
faqs.a: Written notice at least as long as the rent period or three months, whichever is shorter. For a tenant paying monthly that is one month. The tenant gets the same notice rule when leaving.

faqs.q: What notice does a tenant get when the house is foreclosed?
faqs.a: At least 90 days' written notice to vacate, given no sooner than the end of the redemption period, for a tenant whose lease began after the mortgage was signed. A bona fide lease with more than 90 days left can run to its end, unless the new owner will live there.

faqs.q: Does a tenant's death end a Minnesota lease?
faqs.a: Yes, either side can end it on at least two months' written notice effective on the last day of a calendar month. The landlord or the estate's personal representative can send it. The estate still owes rent and restoration costs up to that point.
